data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is inherently less resilient to correlated failure than a large redundant service because the 'Diversity Illusion' masks a shared dependency on common low-level infrastructure (the 'Under-Layer Monoculture').","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services are hosted across physically and politically distinct infrastructure providers.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The services utilize heterogeneous communication protocols that do not share a common routing failure mode.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"While service-level logic is decentralized, the underlying execution environment (e.g., a specific cloud provider's hypervisor, a common DNS root, or a shared BGP routing path) creates a hidden, high-leverage single point of failure. The 'redundancy' in a large service is explicit and managed, whereas the 'diversity' in a decentralized network is superficial, failing to decouple the services from the shared physical or protocol-level substrates.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
